newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi priest held, accused of aiding rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi priest held, accused of aiding rebels.

text.p: Burundian authorities have held a well-known Roman Catholic priest in prison since June, accusing him of helping rebels fighting the Tutsi-led army, his lawyer said on Sunday.

Abbe Patrice Uyiyingoma denied allegations that he had organised the supply of food and medicines to the rebels in Buhinyuza commune, 225 km (140 miles) north of Bujumbura, lawyer Fabien Segatwa told reporters.
Segatwa said he had pressed unsuccessfully for the release of Abbe Uyiyingoma, 44, pending trial. The offences he is accused of carry a penalty of up to 20 years' imprisonment, the lawyer said.
Roman Catholic sources in Bujumbura said the accusation against the priest was a matter of serious concern for the church.
Church sources said there was strong support for Abbe Uyiyingoma, both from his own parishioners and from members of the clergy elsewhere in Burundi.
No other priest is known to be held in Burundi, where the army seized power in a coup in July, on such serious accusations.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi since the killing of its first freely-elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye in 1993. Many of the dead are civilians caught in the the civil war between the military and Hutu rebels.
